title: Neural Barrier Certificates Synthesis of NN-Controlled Continuous Systems via Counterexample-Guided Learning
problem: Efficiently generating and verifying barrier certificates for closed-loop systems with neural network controllers to guarantee safety, particularly for high-dimensional systems where traditional verification approaches are computationally prohibitive.
motivation: Neural network controllers are increasingly deployed in safety-critical applications, but formal verification of their safety properties remains challenging and computationally expensive.
method: The approach employs counterexample-guided learning to synthesize barrier certificate candidates, then verifies them using Sum-Of-Squares (SOS) methods. Instead of invoking SMT solvers, the verification step solves three Linear Matrix Inequality (LMI) constraint feasibility problems, significantly reducing computational cost while maintaining formal guarantees.
key_novelty: Combining counterexample-guided learning with LMI-based verification for barrier certificates, eliminating expensive SMT solver calls and enabling practical verification of high-dimensional NN-controlled systems.
contributions: Novel framework integrating counterexample-guided learning with barrier certificate synthesis
Efficient LMI-based verification procedure replacing SMT solver verification
Demonstrated efficiency and scalability improvements enabling high-dimensional system verification

metrics.other: efficiency and scalability in verifying high-dimensional systems

primary_theme: Formal verification of neural network controlled systems
